docs.title: 8.1 Glossary / List of Abbreviations Asset Management & Pension Administration
docs.text:
Term Abbreviation Description Hedge ratio, protection percentage (afdekkingspercentage, beschermingspercentage) The extent to which the interest rate sensitivity of benefits projected on the basis of personal assets is hedged. General Pension Fund (Algemeen Pensioenfonds) APF General Pension Fund (APF): An APF is a pension provider that can bundle different pension schemes of different employers and industries in one administration. Asset service provider See: Investment administrator. Bank Identifier Code BIC Bank Identifier Code. For example, of ABN: ABNANL2A BIC Correspondent A BIC correspondent is the BIC code of a correspondent bank; a bank that provides services to other banks. Investment administrator (beleggingsadministrateur) BA An independent party that keeps the investment administration for the pension provider. This is a service that is often provided by the custodian. Investments method (beleggingen methode) The calculation of the protection return takes place outside the domain of the pension administration organisation, on the basis of the actual interest rate risk hedge. Investment fund (beleggingsfonds) An investment product with its own fund structure, in which several investors participate. An investment fund may be tradable through a trading platform, but need not be. See also: Investment product. Investment fund (beleggingsfonds) An investment product with its own fund structure, whether or not tradable through a trading platform. Investment instruction (beleggingsinstructie) Investment order. Investment order (beleggingsorder) An instruction to purchase certain investments. Investment pool (beleggingspool) An investment pool is a collection of investments in various funds or mandates that share a common characteristic. An example of this is the 'return-seeking assets investment pool' (zakelijke waarden), which invests in several return-seeking assets funds and/or mandates. Investment pools are intended to bundle and manage the investments of a group of investors. They offer investors the opportunity to diversify and spread risks by investing in different assets. Investment product (beleggingsproduct) Umbrella term for everything that can be invested in. An investment fund and a mandate are both an investment product. Investment product (beleggingsproduct) Umbrella term for everything that can be invested in: investment funds, mandates, and both liquid and illiquid investments. The term is used where it concerns what is actually invested in, as distinct from the investment pool, which is the administrative unit above it. See §4.2. Protection portfolio (beschermingsportefeuille) Specific part of the investment portfolio held with the aim of (mainly) generating the protection return. In the SPR this may be an operational part of the total portfolio through which the interest rate hedge is implemented. When actual protection return is used, it will be one or more separate portfolios. Protection return (beschermingsrendement)

The asset credit that ensures that the future pension benefits and current pension benefits to be financed from the accumulated pension assets remain nominally stable to the extent that they are protected, which is financed from the total return achieved and allocated to the assets depending on maturity on the basis of market valuation, applying allocation rules.

SPR allocation rules are determined:

either on the basis of the change in the interest rate term structure made available by the supervisor (RTS) or directly from the return on the investments designated for that purpose. (Investments method)

See also: Investments method and Interest rate term structure method.

Book of records

A designation for accounting administrations within asset management. Within the framework of this report, this concerns:

ABOR = Accounting Book of Records (main administration, according to accounting rules),

IBOR = Investment Book of Records (often shadow administration).

Cohorts (cohorten)

The term refers to target groups. These can be composed in all kinds of ways. Age target groups, but differentiation is also possible by, for example, active participant, deferred participant, retired, occupationally disabled and/or type of employment

A cohort can be the basis on which a pension provider links participants to an appropriate rebalancing system.

Cohort pool (cohortenpool / cohortpool) Discontinued term. Up to and including release 2026, this referred to the collection of investments (investment pools) for one cohort, as a separate administrative layer between cohort and investment pool. As of release 2027, the FPR model no longer has that layer: the PUO aggregates the changes at participant level per cohort and translates them directly into orders in one or more investment pools. See §4.2. Collective payout phase (collectieve uitkeringsfase) CVP (also: CVU) Phase within a flexible premium scheme (FPR) in which pension benefits are financed collectively. The CVP can be set up unitized (administered in units, integrated with the accumulation phase through netting) or non-unitized (as a separate EUR pot with its own cash flows). Collective payout phase (collectieve uitkeringsfase) CVU See: Collective payout phase (CVP). CVU is a common alternative abbreviation for the same concept. Custodians Custodian of the managed assets of a pension provider. Independently determines the valuation and the return of the holdings and investment portfolios/pools. Defined Benefit DB Pension scheme in which the benefit is promised in advance. Not in scope of the VBPUO standard, but relevant as a frame of reference for the calculation methods of cash flows. Defined Contribution DC Pension scheme in which the contribution is fixed and the benefit depends on the investment result. SPR and FPR are both DC schemes. Direct (actual) protection return (direct, feitelijk beschermingsrendement)

Return generated with one or more direct protection portfolios for interest rate risk.

There are two options here:

With one protection portfolio: the crediting per participant takes place on the basis of the theoretical protection return, with the result being ‘scaled’ to the result of the protection portfolio.

Example: if the total theoretical protection return were 1000 but the actual protection return only 900, each participant is credited with 90% of the theoretical protection return.

With several protection portfolios: an allocation to the protection portfolios applies per age cohort (possibly including inflation instruments).

Fiduciary manager (fiduciair manager) FM A fiduciary manager is responsible for the integral direction of the asset management, in which the (strategic) investment policy of the fund is implemented in the broad sense. In doing so, various underlying asset managers may then be directed. The FM will also keep a (shadow) investment administration. Flexible Premium Scheme (flexibele premieregeling) FPR Defined contribution agreement in which the contribution is invested individually and in which the capital resulting from the contribution is used from the retirement date to finance a variable benefit or to purchase a fixed benefit. Foreign Exchange Rate FX-rate

Exchange rate

An investment currency value of 1.1 USD with an investment-pool currency value of 1 leads to a value in euros of 1/1.1 = € 0.9090

Projected pension benefits (geprojecteerde pensioenuitkeringen) The expected variable benefits in a solidarity defined contribution agreement of a pension provider, based on the accumulated assets designated for pension. The level of the expected variable benefit is determined by applying a projection return to the assets designated for pension This may be higher or lower than the risk-free interest rate. The precise interpretation of projected benefits is a matter of agreement between the parties/governance. Identifier A key data item that uniquely identifies an investment instrument, for example ISIN or SEDOL. Instruction Date Date on which the investment order/investment instruction is sent by the pension administration organisation. International Securities Identification Number ISIN A code number for a “security”, consisting of a country code and a unique National Security Number (NSIN). ISIN is the acronym of International Securities Identification Number. ISIN codes are only used for listed investment funds. In pension asset management practice, administrative pools that do NOT have an ISIN are usually used. Such pools do, however, need a unique identifier. DNB annual statement asset management costs (DNB-jaarstaat kosten vermogensbeheer) J402 Asset management costs broken down into various (investment) categories. The annual statement covers all asset management costs, both the invoiced costs and the costs deducted from the gross returns achieved. Management fees, performance fees and transaction costs are reported per investment category. Leading investment administration (leidende beleggingsadministratie) Investment administration that, for the pension administration organisation and the pension provider, is the basis for (changes in) the personal assets designated for pension benefits (SPR), the capital designated for pension (FPR) and for reporting to the supervisor. Liability-Driven Investment managers LDI Parties that specialise in managing investments with the primary objective of hedging future liabilities or obligations of an investor or institution. LDI mandate (LDI-mandaat) A customised investment portfolio with which the LDI manager or asset manager hedges the interest rate risk of the benefit and accrual entitlements, according to predetermined guidelines, in order to realise the protection return in accordance with the risk-free term definitions of the Wtp framework. Lifecycle The aim of investing according to a lifecycle is to reduce large fluctuations in capital accumulation as the investment horizon approaches. To achieve this, pension providers divide participants into sub-populations based on the remaining time until the retirement date. As the retirement date and investment horizon approach, the investment and interest rate risk for these sub-populations is reduced. This ensures that the investment policy suits the life stage the participant is in. Local currency / Local price (local valuta / local price) Price of the investment instrument in its original currency. Lookthrough This term refers to the "look-through" to the actual investments. Depending on the type of product and the composition of the investments, this "look-through" can be achieved easily, or only with difficulty or at considerable cost. For SPR products, the investment mix cannot be determined at individual level. For FPR products, the investments can in some cases be linked directly to a listed fund. Mandate (mandaat) An investment mandate given to an asset manager to manage a portfolio according to guidelines and risk limits agreed in advance (laid down in an Investment Management Agreement or investment guidelines), not accessible to other investors; positions, costs and risks are directly attributable to the client. Net asset value NAV See: Total Market Value. Netting (netten) Combining (netting/consolidating) or adding up investment orders in the same investment product. Order date Instruction Date Excess return (overrendement) The balance of the total return achieved on the investments, the development of life expectancy and the mortality result, and the allocated protection return on the basis of the allocation rules. Pension fund (pensioenfonds) Institutions that manage and administer pension schemes for employees who work at a specific company or in a specific industry. Pension provider (pensioenuitvoerder)

In the Netherlands, various parties are defined as "pension provider" under the Pensions Act.

In 2023 this concerns/concerned: pension funds, pension insurers, premium pension institutions (PPIs) and General Pension Fund (APF).

Pension scheme (pensioenregeling) A pension scheme under the Pensions Act is an agreement (or commitment) between an employer and an employee that lays down which pension benefits are promised and under which conditions. Pension scheme rules (pensioenreglement) The rules drawn up by the pension provider that describe the rights and obligations of the participant and the pension provider.

Pension

administration organisation (pensioenuitvoeringsorganisatie)

PUO/PA Administrator of pension schemes. Pension insurer (pensioenverzekeraar) Insurance companies that offer individual and collective pension insurance and manage and administer the pension schemes. Portfolio An investment portfolio, i.e. a collection of shares and other securities. Premium pension institution (premiepensioeninstelling) PPI Financial institutions that offer individual defined contribution agreements, in which the level of the pension depends on the contributions paid in and the return on them. Premium-benefit agreement (premie-uitkeringsovereenkomst) Defined contribution agreement carried out by an insurer in which the contribution is invested individually, in which the contribution or the capital resulting from the contribution may be used in the last 15 years before the retirement age to purchase a fixed benefit from the retirement date, and in which the remaining capital is used from the retirement date to finance a variable benefit or to purchase a fixed benefit. Projection return (projectierendement) The future return applied for determining variable benefits. Rebalancing (rebalancen) Periodically or on request bringing an investment portfolio back into balance with the target weights within that portfolio, after inflow into or outflow from the portfolio concerned (external cause) or because there are undesired deviations from the benchmark policy within the portfolio due to market movements. Reconciliation (reconciliatie) The process of comparing whether the (totals of) records of holdings between the various parties (for example asset manager and custodian) are in agreement and, if not, resolving the differences. Interest rate term structure method (rentetermijnstructuur methode) RTS In the RTS method, the SPR protection return is calculated on the basis of the change in the RTS in the shadow VPV. The shadow VPV is the VPV of the shadow entitlements on the basis of the capital present. Solidarity reserve (solidariteitsreserve) A collective asset reserve with which, in a solidarity defined contribution agreement, financial windfalls or setbacks can be shared with future accrual. Risk-sharing reserve (risicodelingsreserve) A collective asset reserve with which, in a flexible defined contribution agreement, financial windfalls or setbacks can be shared with future accrual. Settlement date Date on which the full cycle of the investment order - from the trade date - has been settled. Each (investment) product has its own settlement period, varying from T+1 to T+4 (T = trade date) Solidarity Premium Scheme (solidaire premieregeling) SPR

Premium scheme in which the contribution is invested collectively, the results are in any case allocated by age cohort, and in which the assets designated for pension benefits are used during the payout phase to finance a variable benefit.

For the cohorts, the pension providers must provide for an allocation policy towards the individuals/participants who belong to a cohort.

Allocation policy / Allocation rules (toedelingsbeleid / toedelingsregels) The way in which the pension provider allocates the return to the (groups / cohorts and from those groups to individual) participants. Total market value

The net value of an investment.

For the FPR, this is the value of a share or other form of participation in the total capital.

For the SPR, the investment administrator passes on the value (NAV) of the total capital of the (collective) investment to the pension administration organisation.

Trade date Date on which the pension administration organisation wants the order for a pension scheme (scheme) to be executed. Indirect (theoretical) protection return (indirect, theoretisch beschermingsrendement) Protection against interest rate risk in the solidarity premium scheme by using an interest rate term structure as referred to in Article 2, second paragraph, of the Decree on the Financial Assessment Framework for Pension Funds (Besluit financieel toetsingskader pensioenfondsen). Transfer agent

Registrar; the party that keeps track of the participations. Particularly important for daily tradable holdings (in FPR)

A transfer agent is a trust company, bank or similar institution designated to keep the financial records of an investor and to keep track of the account balance of each investor. Examples are: Fundsettle, Allfunds and BBH).

Valuation date Date of the valuation of the investment pool, used when passing on the value of a (pool) unit within this pool. Value date Value date (valutadatum). A date within an instruction to make a payment. Asset manager (vermogensbeheerder) VB Issuer of financial products (structured products) responsible for active and/or passive portfolio management. Virtual pool (virtuele pool) Designation for a collection of investments that is treated administratively as a single whole. The term is not defined within the VB-PUO standard and is not used in it; for the data exchange, all that matters is that it is an investment product in which an investment pool can invest. Included because the term occurs in practice. See also: Investment product, Mandate. Provision for pension liabilities (voorziening pensioenverplichtingen) VPV The capital required to be able to meet current and future pension obligations. Self-administering fund (zelf uitvoerend fonds) ZAF A pension fund that carries out the pension administration and the asset management wholly or largely in-house, instead of outsourcing them to a pension administration organisation (PUO). In the process flows of this standard, PUO also includes the ZAF.

docs.title: 8.2 Glossary of Data Exchange Based on Standards
docs.text:
Term Meaning API An application programming interface (API) is a structured and documented interface for communication between applications. For more and more organisations, APIs (library of web services) play the key role in offering transactions, distributing content or opening up a workflow between links in the chain. Attribute (attribuut) A unique characteristic or data item of an entity. Understandability of data (begrijpelijkheid gegeven)

Source: NORA

The extent to which data can easily be read and interpreted by users.

Message (bericht) A message describes the interface between two automated applications that exchange messages. Message schema (berichtschema) A message/product definition in schema form. Message structure (berichtstructuur) On the basis of the building block set of entities, attributes etc., one or more hierarchical structures are specified. This structure indicates the relationships between the entities. Consistency of data (consistentie gegevens)

Source: NORA

The extent to which data are free of contradiction and are coherent with other data.

CSV file (CSV-bestand) A data file whose values are separated by a punctuation mark (usually a comma or semicolon), as a specification for table files. The values can be read into a spreadsheet or database program and then presented as a table on a screen. Data Exchange Data Exchange is the technique whereby the data of different automated applications can be exchanged with each other in an automated way on the basis of agreements made on, among other things, standards. Data Governance A system that applies interoperability components (standards and policy rules) to guarantee the acceptable use and high quality of data within a specific ecosystem. Manages the availability, usability, consistency, integrity and security of the data used. Entity (entiteit) This is ‘something that has an existence’. In other words, something that matters, that can be identified, can be named and has value. For example, a person is an entity and can be described with attributes such as first name, surname or BSN number (unique personal number). Data item (gegeven)

Source: NORA

Representation of a fact, concept or instruction, suitable for transfer, interpretation or processing by a person or device.

Data group (entity) (gegevensgroep) Group of data elements that logically belong together. Data quality (gegevenskwaliteit, datakwaliteit)

Source: NORA

The extent to which a set of properties and characteristics of one or more data items meets requirements.

The aim is for data quality to be "fit-for-purpose"; that it matches the use. Quality relates to the extent to which expectations are met.

Data portability (gegevensoverdraagbaarheid) Data portability. The ability to move data easily between interoperable applications and domains. Interoperability (interoperabiliteit)

Interoperability is the ability of organisations (and their processes and systems) to share information with their environment effectively and efficiently.

The European Interoperability Framework distinguishes three forms of interoperability:

  1. Technical interoperability – In order to connect systems, agreements must be made on interfaces, standards and protocols for communication, message formats, data integration, security, availability, etc.

  2. Semantic interoperability – The information that parties exchange must be mutually understandable. The context and meaning of data must be laid down unambiguously.

  3. Organisational interoperability – In order to deliver joint services, organisations must be aligned with each other in terms of their business goals, division of responsibilities and exchange processes.

Interface (koppelvlak) The set of common agreements that makes the exchange of data between digital systems possible. Quality requirement or norm (kwaliteitseis, norm)

Source: NORA

A norm that data must meet.

In many cases a quality requirement is expressed as a number, such as a percentage.

Metadata

Source: NORA

Metadata (metagegevens). Data about data.

Metadata are data that describe the characteristics of other data. Storing metadata with, or linking them to, the data to which they relate has the advantage that the data can be found more easily.

Metadata (metagegevens)

Source: NORA

Data that describe the context, content, structure and form of information and its management over time.

Non-repudiation of data (onweerlegbaarheid gegeven)

Source: NORA

Concept used in electronic message exchange, meaning that the sender of a message cannot deny having sent a particular message and that the recipient of a message cannot deny having received the message from the sender in its original state.

Plausibility of data (plausibiliteit gegeven)

Source: NORA

The extent to which data are regarded as true and credible by users.

Precision of data (precisie gegeven)

Source: NORA

The extent to which data are exact or sufficiently distinctive.

Semantics (semantiek)

Source: NORA

The study of the meaning of words and word groups.

Standard (standaard) These are agreements about information or about a process; this can be at the level of both semantic and technical standards. The agreements are often laid down in documents with a recognised status. Standards are maintained by standardisation organisations such as NEN and recommended or made mandatory by, for example, Bureau Forum Standaardisatie. Straight Through Processing (STP) STP is the electronic processing of processes in which successive administrative actions take place with as little human intervention as possible. Transparency (transparantie)

Source: SSI Speelveldanalyse, Innopay & TNO, 1 October 2021

The extent to which persons, groups and organisations have insight into which data relating to themselves are used for which purpose.

Validity of data (validiteit gegevens)

Source: NORA

The extent to which data comply with the expected structure and storage form.

docs.title: 8.3 Components of the Standard Asset Management Pension Administration
docs.text:
Figure 14 below shows what SIVI will lay down for the Standard Asset Management Pension Administration. The table that follows explains the components.

Figure 14 - Components of the standard in context

No. Component of the standard Explanation 1 Principles The main principles for the development, set-up and governance of the standard. 2 Process descriptions Process descriptions are structured descriptions that explain in detail the steps, activities and elements involved in the specific chain processes and information flows. We use these descriptions to provide a clear understanding of how the processes work and which information flows are involved. In this case, the distinction between the flexible and the solidarity premium scheme is particularly relevant. 3 Governance Governance is about organising the community around the standard in the best possible way. It must be clear who decides what is carried out with regard to standards, and who decides how this is carried out. This includes the rules of procedure of the advisory group and any temporary working groups. 4 Maintenance organisation Maintenance covers the management processes around the standards. It comprises all activities aimed at adapting, extending, further developing, making available and keeping available a (set of) messages that always matches the current needs of the stakeholders. 5 Change procedure Changes to the standard affect several stakeholders. The interests of all participating parties are therefore represented in the change procedure. Requests and proposals for changes will be handled according to an agreed procedure. 6 Data specifications

The data specifications describe the meaning of the data elements and their mutual relationships. Data elements are entities, attributes and code lists.

The data specifications include the mapping to AFD 2.0. This makes clear what is missing. For the missing elements, a proposal has been made in AFD 2.0 terms.

7 Basic structure of messages Base message with the basic structure for a set of messages. The basic structure contains a list of the entities/attributes and the associated hierarchical structure. The description of this base message can be used to create a baseline. 8 Cross table of basic structure and messages

A cross table between the basic structure and the messages.

For each message, the table indicates which entities/attributes apply. It also indicates the number of repetitions (entities) and which attributes must be populated. It is also possible to make selections from code lists, i.e. to indicate which code values apply.

9 Message specifications

The specifications are based on the data specifications. In this message specification, this is translated into a hierarchical message structure.

Part of the set of message specifications is the response message. This is the feedback message (§4.4).

Each message has a general section that indicates, among other things, who the sender/recipient of the message is.

10 Message checks A specification of all checks on the messages, for example consistency checks. It is an option to deliver these checks in machine-readable form, but initially this is not necessary. 11 Extension of AFD 2.0 Extension of AFD 2.0 with requested data elements. AFD 2.0 can be extended monthly at the request of stakeholders. 12 Baseline This is the base message that is imported into AOS. After that, AFD definitions can be created. 13 Schemas

JSON Schema or XML Schema per message/basic structure. Among other things, to be able to validate messages.

AOS delivers JSON schemas based on AFD 2.0 messages and AFD definitions.

14 Events manual

Examples of handling specific situations. The situations show how the standard must be applied.

Example messages are part of the events manual.

15 Interface specifications

In automated connections between distributed systems (machine-to-machine), there is an interface that makes communication possible. Such an interface is called a ‘koppelvlak’ in Dutch. The description of an interface is what we call interface specifications.

Examples:

  • Web services

  • File transfer

  • Delivery via a portal

Instructions on (data) security can be part of the interface specifications.

The interface specification for the RESTful API is in §7.4 (OpenAPI).

16 Test facilities

Facilities to support developers in implementing the messages/interface specifications.

This can include a generic set of test data.

17 Calculation rules Instructions for performing calculations. The calculations apply to data elements in the messages.

Message checks/

Consistency checks are recorded in JMESPath and relate to the message for which they have been written. Checks that go beyond a single message, i.e. for which other messages or back-office information are needed, fall outside the scope of these checks

JSON schemas

The JSON schemas are in principle self-explanatory, but some explanation may be useful because these schemas are also split up in JSON technology. This means that, in addition to the expected entities and entity types such as 'party' and 'pension.scheme', certain key elements are also referred to, such as "$defs", "type", "properties", "additionalProperties" and "required".

As of JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 this is called "$defs". In older versions (draft-07, 2019-09) the term "definitions" was used for this.

These properties and specifications that apply to, for example, 'commonFunctional' are not all grouped around 'commonFunctional', but are spread across the JSON schema. The main thing to note is that this spread is not arbitrary, but follows from the different types of properties

docs.title: 8.5 Changes release 2027
docs.text: This section summarises what has changed in this manual compared with release 2026: first what applies to all or several messages, then what changes per message, and finally the structure of the manual. What has been added or changed since the prerelease of 21 July 2026 is shown in red. Section numbers refer to this version. The changes in the JSON schemas are in the release notes.

docs.title: For all or several messages
docs.text:
FPR model and roles

  • One FPR model: the distinction between model 1 (direct order model) and model 2 (layered order model) has been dropped, with one schematic representation (Figure 2). What happens below the investment pool falls outside the data exchange (§4.1, §4.2).
  • The cohort pool as a layer between cohort and investment pool has been discontinued. The PUO aggregates the changes at participant level per cohort and translates them directly into net orders in one or more investment pools; that allocation lies with the PUO and falls outside the data exchange. The investment administrator does not know the strategic allocation within a cohort and administers the investment pools on the instruction of the PUO (§4.2). In the translation table (§8.4), the rows of pension.cohortPool have been dropped.
  • The role ACB (administrator of cohort and investment pools) has been discontinued as an independent actor; in practice the BA or the PUO performs it, and the message schema can still support the role (§6.4). See #131. The roles have been reduced to the four from Figure 8 and 9: PUO, BA, FM/VB and LDI manager.
  • Investment product is the umbrella term for investment funds, mandates and other investments; the investment pool is the administrative layer above it (§4.2, §4.3.5, §6.4). Terms LDI-mandaat and Mandaat added to §8.1; also Beleggingsproduct, Beleggingsfonds and Virtuele pool, the last with the note that the standard does not use that term.
  • For collective premium flows within FPR (risk premiums, reserves, withdrawals), SPR messages 1 to 4 are used (§4.1). See #91. Within FPR, messages 2 and 4 serve for the flows outside the unit administration and message 3 for the interest rate risk profile towards the FM/VB and the LDI manager (§4.3).
  • Return allocation depends on the set-up: for unitized products the return is included in the unit price; for a collective payout provision in euros it runs via message 4 (§4.2).

FPR process flow (Figure 8 and 9, §4.3.1)

  • Figure 8 and 9 are indicative: the times are indicative, the order of the steps is guiding. They show one run of the trading cycle for one administrative set-up; sending to more recipients and additional deliveries have no step of their own. Both figures use the same step letter for the same step.
  • Phase 1 is called order input and covers only T-4; the feedback on T+3 (order confirmation, message 6, and final month-end NAV, message 13) is in phase 3.
  • Phase 3: the LDI manager carries out the transactions on the LDI mandate itself (H1); the FM/VB monitors the LDI manager and handles the other investment portfolios (H2). Figure 8 now also shows this split execution, with the feedback.
  • Figure 9 (non-unitized): the cash instruction for the CVP goes out on T-4, at the same time as the order instruction (was T+3). In the case of a switch the BA sends that instruction, in the case of a complete sell the PUO. The EUR order for the CVP does not go through the order instruction (message 5); the valuation message after the CVP execution has been dropped, and the return reaches the PUO via message 4. The same applies to other collective parts in euros: risk-sharing reserve, compensation deposit, other reserves and provisions.
  • Feedback on executed transactions usually runs via SWIFT, but this is not prescribed and does not apply to all instruments (swaps are handled differently); the channel is a matter of mutual agreement. The channel names have been removed from the diagrams.

Sender and recipient (Table 12, §6.4)

  • Table 12 has new actor columns: Soort, ACB and BR dropped, LDI added. See #99, #119, #121, #98.
  • Sender and recipient follow Figure 1 (SPR) and Figure 8 and 9 (FPR) throughout: in Table 12, in the overview of the message types (§6.4) and in chapter 4. Table 12 is a role matrix: messages 10 and 14 are sent by the BA, and by the PUO only if it performs the role of BA itself. See #142. The changes per message are listed below.
  • Principle: information received is not forwarded, so the sender sends the same message to each recipient separately, with its own endpoint and identification. The purpose can differ per recipient: the same order instruction is an instruction for one and a notification for the other (§2.4).

Reserves and provisions (§6.3)

  • Division of roles: refKey identifies, reserveType (AFDRES) classifies and is the key for the investment policy, reserveDescription describes. See #111.
  • Code list AFDRES extended with codes 9 to 15. Where investment policy is shared, consolidation is possible; a separate code only for a separate investment policy. Applies to SPR and FPR. See #134.
  • If reserveIndicator = true, reserveType is mandatory; reserveDescription is desirable for 99 (Other) and possible for the other codes.
  • The reserve fields are only in the cohort, not on the investment portfolio.

Other rules

  • Cohorts with value 0 may be sent with 0 or omitted. See #100. The rule is in §6.3 and applies to all messages with cohorts (1 to 4), including reserves and provisions; omitting a reserve does not automatically mean that the value is 0. The standard does not recognise a field without a value (null).
  • messageId is unique across all messages and does not serve for grouping or bundling; the exception is chunking (§6.3, §7.6). See #108.
  • Date conventions for startDate and projectionDate (§6.3, §3.2.1, §3.2.3). See #94.
  • APFs with several ring-fenced compartments (kringen): two common scenarios for the PUV codes (§6.3, §6.4.1). See #114.
  • participationStatus (ADNDNS): value 60 removed from the documentation, in line with the schema. See #103 and #71.
  • Chunking: the standard has no maximum number of chunks; limits are agreements between chain parties (§2.7). See #127. chunkMeta.default is called chunking.default in the documentation, in line with the schemas.
  • The funding ratio falls outside the scope (§2.3). See #118.
  • Digital signing (x-jws-signature) and authentication with an API key (x-api-key) are options, not obligations; only OAuth 2.0 is mandatory, in line with the OAS (§2.7, §7.4). The limits in the schemas are binding (§2.7).
  • afdDefinitionName has a fixed value in each schema, equal to the file name with 001.00; this also applies to the feedback message (in the prerelease …-001.02-…) (§7.5.1.1). See #140. afdDefinitionVersion remains 001.05 for the ten messages and 001.02 for the feedback message, the same numbers as in the prerelease.

docs.title: Per message
docs.text:
Message 1 Assets (0001a) has no changes of its own beyond the rules above (cohorts with value 0, reserves and provisions).

Messages 2, 3 and 4: SPR and FPR route

  • The prerelease laid down two mutually exclusive population patterns for message 2, with an exclusion rule as a consistency check (§6.3.1). See #113. The exclusion between the cash flow directly under the scheme and the cash flow per investment portfolio has been dropped; the breakdowns per cohort and per investment portfolio continue to exclude each other in messages 2 and 3. The routes for messages 2, 3 and 4 are set out together in the new §3.2.5, with Figure 1a, 1b, 9a and 9b: in message 2 the breakdown is optional, in message 3 there is exactly one; in message 4 the investment portfolio applies to both routes, without route exclusion. The cash flow and the payments directly under the scheme apply in both routes; in the FPR route they as a rule contain the total of the portfolios.
  • Consistency checks (§6.3.1): sum checks for a cohort breakdown, and the concept of reconciliation explained. A scheme in message 2 contains at least one cash flow (direct, per cohort or per investment portfolio). The technical safeguarding via (..)-validationRules.json has not yet been modelled.

Message 2 Cashflow (0001b)

  • In each cash flow block, netAmount and netDate are mandatory and the amounts and dates of inflow and outflow optional; the money changes hands on the netDate (§6.3).
  • The message carries an expected or an established net cash flow. Timing and frequency are chain agreements; what is fixed, however, is that an established statement follows the settlement of the unit sale, because the amount arises from it (§4.3.1, §4.3.2).
  • Own section in chapter 4, with the purpose, the FPR population pattern and the relationship with messages 5, 10 and 14 (§4.3.2). In Table 12 the BA is also a sender.

Message 3 Pension Projection (0001c)

  • A portfolio branch for the FPR route, with its own section in chapter 4 (§4.3.3).
  • The payments under the cohort and under the investment portfolio are optional (0..*, O); an empty list financialTransaction no longer needs to be included (§6.4.4, §6.5).

Message 4 Return Information (00002)

  • Total return and the breakdown into matching and return may be included in one message, distinguished via refKey (§3.2.4). See #109.
  • Own section in chapter 4, with the demarcation from message 13. Its use depends on the set-up: with a unitized CVP it is not needed, with a CVP in euros it is, because message 13 has no unit value there (§4.3.4).

Messages 5 Order Instruction (00541) and 6 Order Confirmation (00542)

  • Switch convention: the code switch in buySellId has been replaced by switchfrom and switchto; the direction follows from buySellId, amounts are always positive. switchType and financialInformationRef are also in message 6. See #115. switchType has the codes of AFDSWI (1, 2) instead of the labels sequential and one-day.
  • Message 5: per trade instruction exactly one of tradeAmount and tradeQuantity. See #116. In a switch, exactly one leg per switch pair carries the amount or the quantity, and the other leg neither; in practice the switchfrom leg carries the number of units on the transition to the collective payout phase. The consistency checks of messages 5 and 6 are in the new §6.3.2.
  • Message 6: tradeQuantity, tradePrice, counterparty, broker, interestAmount, commissionAmount, clearingBroker and clearingBrokerCashAccount are optional; tradeAmount remains mandatory. See #105. If tradeQuantity and tradePrice are both present, quantity × price = amount applies (§6.3.2).
  • The order instruction goes from the PUO to the BA, the order confirmation back from the BA to the PUO. The provider of the fund, which carries out the ordering in the underlying investments, is a different role from the order-processing party (§4.3.5, §4.3.6). In §6.4 the designation Direct order has been dropped.

Message 10 Control Information Investment Pools (00553)

  • The cohortPool layer has been removed; the data are directly on investment.pool (§6.4.8). A formal FPR decision has not been found in the minutes; the change has been made in the absence of known objections. See #124.
  • dummyCashId, tradeQuantity, unitPrice and currencyExchangeRate removed from investment.pool; buySellId, tradeValueAmount and currencyType remain. See #133.
  • Explanation of the purpose, with the translation from message 5 to message 10: netting per investment pool, conversion of units into amounts and the treatment of switches (§4.3.7). The permitted values of buySellId are sell; buy.

Message 13 Value Information Investment Pool (00555b)

  • marketValueAmount removed from investment.pool; the net asset value runs only via preliminaryUnitValueAmount. Field descriptions merged. See #128. The description of participationValuationDate has been updated; the attribute remains mandatory.
  • Own explanation: the message delivers the price information on T-4 and the final month-end NAV on T+3, and is the basis for reconciliation and payment information (§4.3.8).

Message 14 Payment Information (00556)

  • Several payments per scheme in one message, at least one and at most 999, instead of one message per payment (§4.3.9, §6.4). See #149.
  • Sent by the BA to the FM; the PUO sends it only if it performs the role of BA itself, and is no longer listed as sender in Table 12. Explanation of purpose and meaning (§4.3.9).
  • collectionAccountIban has a maximum of 34 characters, the international IBAN length according to ISO 13616 (was 10) (§6.3). See #135.

Message 15 Corporate Actions (00557)

  • New message, with a process explanation for passing on corporate actions from the asset management chain to the PUO (§4.3.10). See #87. It is an ad hoc message outside the trading run and is therefore not in Figure 8 and 9. It relates to investment funds that are traded directly on a trading platform; corporate actions do not apply to investment pools themselves. The sender is the FM or the BA.
  • Code list AFDCOA (formerly AFDCAE) for corporateActionType: 1 Cash dividend, 2 Stock dividend, 3 Product change, 99 Other. A rebate falls under 99 (in the prerelease: rebate); a separate code is not yet available. See #137. The amount of a rebate is in cashDividendTotalAmount and/or cashDividendPerUnitAmount.
  • Message 15 is an exception to the rule that changes within an investment product do not affect the PUO: the PUO does have to process dividend, rebate and unit changes (§4.2).
  • The empty financialInformation.reportingPeriod has been removed from the message.

Feedback Message

  • A duplicate messageId is rejected with HTTP 400 and a feedback message in the response body (§4.4). See #129. Chunking is the exception to this.
  • party.sender and party.receiver in the description of commonTechnical. See #90.
  • More scenarios for successful and failed processing; errorCodeExplanation a maximum of 1000 characters (was 300). See #107.
  • Orders that cannot be executed are reported back with the feedback message (status Rejected, error code, description); force majeure falls under bilateral agreements (§4.4). See #132.
  • originalMessageType also includes 00542. See #126. The list of values follows the ten active messages: 00557 added, the discontinued messages removed; also in the figure in §4.4.

Discontinued messages 7, 8, 9, 11 and 12

  • Removed from the active message set; the numbering of the other messages is unchanged. See #99, #119, #121. They are in one block at the end of chapter 4, with the reason per message (§4.3.11), and no longer in §6.4.

docs.title: Structure of the manual
docs.text:
• Chapter 4 has been reorganised: the use of SPR messages within FPR is at the end of the introduction (§4.1); the process flow has its own section (§4.3.1); each active message has a section, now including messages 2, 3 and 4 (§4.3.2 to §4.3.10); the discontinued messages are in §4.3.11; the feedback message is §4.4. In §6.4 the message structures have been renumbered consecutively: message 10 is §6.4.8, through to the feedback message, §6.4.12.
  • The tables with the basic message structure and the maximum numbers in §6.4.1 are generated from the model. They show the hierarchy per location: an entity that occurs in several places appears there several times, each under its own parent. For financialTransaction.payment the three maxima (999, 9999 or 99999) are shown with the place where they apply. §6.4 explains the suffixes (such as _1) in the message diagrams on GitHub.
  • §6.5 Cross-reference: readable headings, a filter by message and one block per entity and parent.
  • The example messages are in a separate folder Voorbeeldberichten per release on GitHub, no longer in the message folders; main is leading there. For release 2027 they have been supplemented for all messages, based on situations from practice with existing pension providers and fictitious data (§7.5).
  • Figure 3 (§4.2) shows ages instead of years of birth.
  • References: internal references that led nowhere have been fixed, with a check that monitors this from now on; GitHub references point to the Stichting SIVI repository; references to GitHub issues placed with the text; spelling of technical names harmonised.
  • The colophon summarises the changes; this section is new.
  • Some textual improvements.
